questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a feature of organisational buying?
questions.explanation: Emotional decision-making is more common in household buying, while organisational buying relies on rational and structured processes.

questions.stem: In an organisational buying decision, who is typically responsible for negotiating the purchase?
questions.explanation: The buyer is the person responsible for negotiating the terms of the purchase and placing the order.

distractorRationale.a: The initiator suggests the need but does not negotiate.
distractorRationale.b: The influencer provides input but does not handle negotiations.
distractorRationale.c: The decider approves the purchase but does not negotiate.

questions.stem: What distinguishes a new-task buy from a modified rebuy?

options.text: New-task buys are for first-time purchases.

questions.explanation: A new-task buy is characterized by the purchase of a product for the first time, requiring thorough evaluation.

distractorRationale.a: New-task buys often involve unfamiliar products.
distractorRationale.b: Modified rebuys typically involve previously purchased items, requiring less research.
distractorRationale.d: Cost can vary and is not a defining feature of modified rebuys.
